newsitem.title: USA: Clinton-Yeltsin summit set - Helsinki March 20-21.
newsitem.headline: Clinton-Yeltsin summit set - Helsinki March 20-21.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin will hold their next summit in Helsinki on March 20-21, it was announced on Friday.

"We have now agreed that President Clinton and President Yeltsin will meet in Helsinki on March 20 and 21," (U.S.) Vice President Al Gore said at a joint news conference with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin. Although it was the U.S. turn to host the summit on its soil, officials said it had been moved to Finland, which borders Russia, in deference to health problems that have been burdening Yeltsin.

"This of course will be an important meeting. We expect among other things that the presidents will address bilateral arms control, European security and a number of economic issues of importance to our peoples," Gore said.

The two spoke during a periodic meeting of a Cabinet-level Russian-American liaison group which they chair, and just before Chernomyrdin was to confer at the White House with Clinton. The Russian said through a translator that the liaison group meeting had been highly productive.

"I can say this work has been productive as we have prepared more than 40 documents for signature on the most important issues between our two countries," Chernomyrdin said, without offering detail on the issues involved. Of the summit, he said, "I do hope that the solutions that the two presidents will reach at that summit will be extremely important for all of us ... The agenda will include the most topical issues for our two nations."
